composition_answer: NOT_YET. The committed authority chain, input identity, arithmetic semantics, and surface separation are sound and fully verified: the eight atomic ID-weight-output triples are byte-identical to the accepted representative expert-output reuse authorization (sha256 1b8b053d60f87c9da8c8c81a41a3d82f7652859a2464941c39b5a1eab3d7c070, independently ACCEPTED at review sha256 54d559fe39c13152c2c368fa1f99a219c167178b06d58f47bb46822af33b46bc) and to the COMPLETE real expert execution evidence (sha256 fe1cad02405b74d9000afec915bdf7e772e6dd77c13b7e4cc5b5db35606b51e4), in canonical order [250,10,237,62,73,177,218,28] with expert 62 (ordinal 3, weight 0.23688715675086147) before expert 73 (ordinal 4, weight 0.2514906203405492) despite 73's larger weight, so any independent weight sort is excluded and the prohibited historical direct-DPREFIX ordering and output (6479a8352a355d5f979172bc19038d44b4df992925fab427d2caeaf24445efdc) are explicitly rejected. The frozen arithmetic contract pins the canonical F017 proof/reference surface exactly as protected by the committed perturbation doctrine (M_k = python_fsum_i(q_i*f64(e_i[k]))): exact f32-to-f64 promotion via struct.unpack, one binary64 multiplication per term under roundTiesToEven, a direct CPython 3.14.6 math.fsum call on the ordered tuple of eight binary64 products per coordinate, little-endian f64[6144] serialization, fail-closed on environment drift before input consumption, and forbids serial-f32, product casts, reordering, BLAS, parallel reduction, GPU, and alternate fsum implementations; this is correctly and unambiguously classified as intentionally distinct from the production selected_slot_rank_order_serial_binary32_reduction runtime, which remains unauthorized. Consumption semantics are sufficient: open-directory-once, O_NOFOLLOW leaf opens relative to the validated directory descriptor, fstat before/after with device-inode identity, regular-file, nlink==1, read-only mode, exact 24576-byte size, finiteness, private-manifest verification before outputs, and EXPECTED=BEFORE=CONSUMED=AFTER where the consumed bytes ARE the validated first-read bytes from the same descriptor, making validate-then-consume races moot. The synthetic rehearsal uses full real geometry with no real representative bytes and its output was independently reproduced bit-identically in two additional fresh processes by this review. The preparation performed zero aggregate executions, ledger 175->175, zero checkpoint/shard/expert work, and stops AFTER_ROUTED_AGGREGATE_ONLY. HOWEVER, the authorization is not yet sufficient to permit the future checkpoint-free routed-aggregate execution, because the committed execution surface has two required gate defects: (1) the --synthetic-rehearsal mode skips the representative output-identity check and the private-manifest check while accepting an arbitrary --output-root, so a crafted synthetic manifest carrying the eight public real output SHAs pointed at the retained package root would compute and serialize the real protected aggregate with zero approved releases while reporting aggregate_executions 0, falsifying the authorization's claim that a future approved single-use release is required for the real surface; and (2) the --execute path has no durable attempt-start or release-consumption mechanism, so the pinned future_aggregate_execution_count of 1 and the GO_EXECUTE_ONCE_NO_RETRY disposition are unenforced by committed bytes (one approved release could drive unlimited re-runs, and the atomic writer silently overwrites a prior event artifact), a regression from the accepted expert-recovery event's DURABLE_ATTEMPT_START_BEFORE_EXPERT_COMPUTATION token burn. Both are localized executor fixes; once remediated and re-reviewed, this authorization structure is sufficient to permit exactly one future checkpoint-free routed-aggregate execution over the eight banked representative expert outputs while preserving the intentional distinction from the production serial-f32 surface.

non_blocking_required_findings.title: Synthetic-rehearsal mode can compute the real protected aggregate without any release
non_blocking_required_findings.detail: In --synthetic-rehearsal mode, validate_records(synthetic=True) deliberately skips the output_sha256 == OUTPUT_SHAS identity check, OpenOnceInputs is invoked with manifest_sha=None so the private-manifest binding is not enforced, and --output-root is unconstrained. The synthetic leaf filenames are forced to the exact real retained filenames ({ii}-expert-{id}-down.f32le). A synthetic-input manifest listing the eight real output SHA-256 values (public in the committed authorization) pointed at the retained package root passes every check (regular, nlink==1, read-only, 24576 bytes, sha match, finite) and aggregate_bytes then computes the real routed aggregate, serializes it, and prints its SHA-256 with disposition SYNTHETIC_COMPLETE and aggregate_executions 0. This contradicts the module docstring claim that synthetic rehearsal never resolves the retained representative package, contradicts executor.future_approved_single_use_release_required=true, and miscounts a real aggregate computation as zero. The committed rehearsal generator itself is clean (fresh temp directory, synthetic bytes only); the defect is that the executor does not enforce the isolation the docstring and authorization claim.
non_blocking_required_findings.required_remediation: In synthetic mode, fail closed if any record's declared output_sha256, or any consumed input's computed SHA-256, is a member of OUTPUT_SHAS (the executor already carries these constants), and optionally reject an --output-root containing a manifest.json whose SHA-256 equals MANIFEST_SHA.

non_blocking_required_findings.title: No committed exactly-once enforcement for the single future --execute event
non_blocking_required_findings.detail: validate_release checks schema, exact key set, INDEPENDENTLY_APPROVED status, authorization and executor SHA bindings, and GO_EXECUTE_ONCE_NO_RETRY disposition, but the executor writes no durable attempt-start before computation and never consumes or burns the release, so the same approved release file can drive unlimited --execute runs; _atomic_write's os.replace also silently overwrites a previously written event artifact. The authorization pins future_aggregate_execution_count=1 and prohibits retry_without_future_release, but no committed mechanism enforces once-ness. The accepted expert-recovery precedent recorded token_consumed_at DURABLE_ATTEMPT_START_BEFORE_EXPERT_COMPUTATION with a durable attempt-start artifact; its absence here is a regression on the same surface class. Because validate_release enforces set(release) == expected_keys exactly, the release document cannot carry additional single-use machinery without an executor change that invalidates the executor SHA binding in this authorization, so this must be resolved before release approval. Severity is bounded by full bit-determinism (any re-run yields byte-identical output) and zero ledger exposure, hence NON_BLOCKING_REQUIRED rather than BLOCKING.
non_blocking_required_findings.required_remediation: Add a durable attempt-start record written and fsynced before aggregate_bytes in --execute mode, fail closed if an attempt-start or terminal output artifact already exists, and refuse to overwrite an existing --output path in --execute mode.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: Release identity fields not value-pinned
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: validate_release requires the keys event_id, release_id, attempt_id, and schema_version to exist but does not pin their values (e.g. event_id == F017-REPRESENTATIVE-ROUTED-AGGREGATE-ANALYTICAL-1, schema_version == 1.0.0). Cross-event substitution is already excluded by the authorization_sha256 and executor_sha256 bindings, so this is hardening only. The release also carries no independent-approval evidence binding (approval sha or token), consistent with prior accepted events where approval evidence is bound at the release-approval stage; the future release approval must supply that binding.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: Committed rehearsal evidence is value-identical but not byte-identical to generator output
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: Re-running the committed generator reproduces every value exactly (manifest sha cdb9a8f60821165326ab861b24c3363eaeed07a1181dfe055960fcd40c957cbb, all eight synthetic input SHAs, and identical fresh-process output sha 9b87bc4559d25cc296b4c48a5670f4ea6504266060ac50c090ccccced307e3ff), but the committed file's JSON arrays were reformatted inline after generation, so byte-level provenance re-derivation of sha256 ac353d30ec4bbd6235726fee4174fecb98fcb21aa095a4fb71cefb18b49b981d from the generator fails. Emit canonical serialization from the generator so committed evidence is byte-reproducible.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: Validator binds adjudication and reuse review by SHA only, and CLI fail-closed path unexercised by fresh process
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: The validator pins the semantic adjudication and the reuse review by exact SHA-256 (sufficient identity; both parsed and confirmed by this review) but does not additionally parse their verdict/classification fields; and the two fresh rehearsal processes exercise only the success path of the executor CLI, with all mutation rejections exercised in-process by the unit tests rather than through a fresh-process FAIL_CLOSED exit-2 invocation. Redundant content assertions and one fresh-process negative invocation would harden both.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: Writable-alias exclusion cannot cover pre-existing foreign write descriptors
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: no_writable_alias is enforced by st_nlink==1 plus mode & 0o222 == 0, which cannot exclude a write-open descriptor already held by another process. This is a kernel-level limit shared with the accepted reuse resolver, and is fully mitigated for correctness because the consumed bytes are the validated first-read bytes (EXPECTED=BEFORE=CONSUMED) and the AFTER re-read detects tampering. Recorded for completeness, no action required.

adjudication.q1_exact_accepted_inputs_atomic_binding_: PASS. The eight atomic triples (ordinal, expert_id, routing_weight, private_relative_path, output_sha256, little-endian-f32, [6144], 24576) in the authorization are value-identical to the accepted reuse authorization's triples (modulo its added semantic_role, checked by the validator's exact reconstruction) and to the join of id_weight_pairs and outputs in the COMPLETE real execution evidence, verified against actual producer bytes, not PASS flags. Canonical order [250,10,237,62,73,177,218,28] holds with 62 before 73; since weight(73)=0.2514906203405492 exceeds weight(62)=0.23688715675086147, order-sensitivity is proven non-vacuous, and both the executor and validator reject the 62/73 swap and weight reassignment (tests confirmed). All eight weights round-trip exactly between the JSON decimals and CPython 3.14.6 binary64 repr.
adjudication.q2_consume_what_you_validated: PASS. Directory opened once (O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW), manifest verified against MANIFEST_SHA before any output open, each leaf opened once with O_NOFOLLOW relative to the validated directory descriptor, fstat on the descriptor (regular, nlink==1, mode&0o222==0, exact 24576), exact-length read with oversize rejection, SHA check, finiteness over all 6144 f32 values, then aggregation consumes the exact validated bytes object and verify_after re-reads the same descriptor requiring device-inode identity and EXPECTED==CONSUMED==AFTER. Relative-path traversal is excluded (Path(name).name == name rejects separators, '.', and '..'). Sufficient; see RRA-C1-D4 for the only residual, mitigated, gap.
adjudication.q3_leakage_exclusion: PASS with RRA-C1-R1 caveat. The executor imports only stdlib (hashlib, json, math, os, stat, struct, sys, tempfile, argparse, platform, pathlib); no numpy/mlx/BLAS/GPU/parallel machinery, no checkpoint, shard, or expert-execution interface exists in any committed path. The historical direct-DPREFIX output SHA is pinned and rejected by the validator, real mode rejects any output substitution against OUTPUT_SHAS, and shared-expert/FFN/residual/S2/production-serial-f32 operations are absent from the executor and prohibited by the authorization. The one leak path found is the synthetic-mode bypass of RRA-C1-R1, which permits the real aggregate itself to be computed outside the release gate; historical or production surfaces still cannot enter the event's inputs.
adjudication.q4_semantic_classification: PASS. The committed perturbation contract protects exactly M_k=python_fsum_i(q_i*f64(e_i[k])) as the routed_aggregate surface with fixed Python-math.fsum-equivalent binary64 accumulation; the routing contract v3-clarified pins the production runtime policy as selected_slot_rank_order_serial_binary32_reduction as a DIFFERENT surface; the accepted frozen aggregate-input contract (sha ec38d793a95894daa71a5179650b91978b4aec44512311aa29a7c5c897b4b872) carries the same separation; and the new adjudication resolves the portability of 'fsum-equivalent' by narrowing to a direct CPython 3.14.6 math.fsum call with all other environments FAIL_CLOSED, which is a valid instance of the protected class, not a substitution. Classification CANONICAL_F017_PROOF_REFERENCE_SURFACE_INTENTIONALLY_DISTINCT_FROM_PRODUCTION_SERIAL_F32 is correct and unambiguous; the production surface remains explicitly NOT_AUTHORIZED_BY_THIS_CONTRACT.
adjudication.q5_exact_arithmetic_bit_determinism: PASS. struct.unpack_from('<f') yields the exact binary32 value as a CPython binary64 (exact promotion; the float() wrap is identity); one binary64 multiplication per term; math.fsum called directly exactly once per coordinate on the ordered 8-tuple (correctly-rounded shewchuk summation, deterministic); struct.pack_into('<d') at 8*k in increasing k gives contiguous little-endian binary64. Environment drift fails closed before input consumption (CPython exactly 3.14.6, little-endian, radix 2, mant_dig 53, rounds 1, Darwin arm64), checked both at main() entry and inside aggregate_bytes. Serial-f32 substitution provably differs (committed test demonstrates nonzero divergence), reordering and weight resorting are rejected, no BLAS/parallel/GPU path exists, and non-finite inputs, products, and sums each fail closed. Bit-determinism was independently confirmed: this review's two additional fresh processes reproduced the committed synthetic output SHA exactly (four identical fresh-process results in total).
adjudication.q6_instantiable_future_impossible_now: PARTIAL FAIL. --execute is impossible under committed bytes alone: it requires a release document with schema pulsarmlx.f017.representative-routed-aggregate-single-use-release, status INDEPENDENTLY_APPROVED, real_event_authorized true, disposition GO_EXECUTE_ONCE_NO_RETRY, and SHA bindings to both the exact authorization bytes and the exact executor bytes; no such document exists anywhere in the repository (verified by search), and the executor requires the authorization to remain in PREPARED_REVIEW_REQUIRED state so the release alone carries the approval. The interface is instantiable under a future approved release. However RRA-C1-R1 shows the real aggregate VALUE is computable today via the synthetic interface, and RRA-C1-R2 shows once-ness and output-overwrite protection are unenforced; both must be fixed for the gate to match its claims.
adjudication.q7_synthetic_rehearsal_adequacy: PASS with RRA-C1-D3 noted. The rehearsal uses the full real geometry (8 inputs, real IDs, real binary64 weights, real filenames, 24576-byte f32[6144] inputs, 49152-byte f64[6144] output) with deterministic synthetic bytes that share no content with the real outputs (real_representative_output_bytes_used false; all synthetic SHAs disjoint from the eight real SHAs). Two fresh pinned-interpreter processes produced byte-identical outputs with exact AFTER hashes, and this review independently regenerated the entire evidence value-for-value including the output SHA. Mutation coverage (order swap, weight reassignment, historical/real substitution, writable alias, hash mismatch, wrong size, non-finite, serial-f32 divergence, 30 validator mutations) is exercised by the committed tests, all 10 passing under the pinned environment when re-run by this review.
adjudication.q8_validator_independence: PASS. The validator pins every load-bearing field by exact equality (ids, statuses, head, classification, all seven SHA bindings with repo byte verification, private package dict, expert input SHA, all eight full triples, historical-output rejection, preflight booleans and surface values, arithmetic contract algorithm/output/forbidden/separation content, executor capability booleans, rehearsal content, future output dict, exact accounting dict, stop boundary, exact prohibition key set all true) and independently reconstructs the producer schemas: it re-derives the reuse authorization's triples from the reviewed triples plus semantic_role and re-joins the execution evidence's id_weight_pairs with its outputs block, requiring exact equality against actual loaded producer bytes. Executor capabilities are enforced via the SHA binding to the reviewed executor bytes, which this review inspected directly.
adjudication.q9_scope_and_accounting: PASS. The authorization permits exactly one FUTURE aggregate execution (future_aggregate_execution_count 1) with zero future checkpoint/shard/expert budget, and this preparation performed zero aggregate executions: accounting pins starting_ledger 175, terminal_ledger 175, all four preparation counters zero; the preparation evidence, adjudication, arithmetic contract, rehearsal, and loop state all record ledger 175 with zero checkpoint/shard/expert/aggregate work; the real-input preflight packet (disposition PRODUCTION_BINDINGS_RESOLVED, inputs 8, all counters zero) was recomputed by this review as a deterministic string whose SHA-256 exactly matches the committed packet_sha256, confirming no aggregation occurred in it; stop_boundary is AFTER_ROUTED_AGGREGATE_ONLY and go_token_in_this_phase is prohibited. Enforcement of the future count of exactly 1 is the subject of RRA-C1-R2.
